audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers treat Spirit's Refuge as a blanket damage block ("nullify your E Toxic Shot auto-attacks entirely", "strip your primary DPS window", "your Q blind and his W auto-block offset each other"). Nothing says what still gets through.
audit.why: Riot's text is specific: "Attacks that would hit Shen or his allies near his spirit blade are blocked." It blocks basic attacks. Blinding Dart is a targeted ability, not an attack, so it lands through the bubble at full effect — which means the correct play inside Spirit's Refuge is to keep casting Q, not to stop poking. The entry currently tells the player to disengage from the one window where his spell still works.
audit.corrected: Spirit's Refuge blocks basic attacks only — Blinding Dart is a spell and lands through it. Poke with Q, just not with autos.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says "his Spirit's Refuge is online every 18 seconds".
audit.why: Spirit's Refuge is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s. The 18 belongs to Shadow Dash (18/16/14/12/10s). The entry has attached his longest cooldown to his shortest-cycling defensive tool, which makes every trade window it recommends too generous by several seconds.
audit.corrected: Spirit's Refuge is 16s at rank 1 and 10s at rank 5; Shadow Dash is the 18-second cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] claims "your Move Quick W guarantees escape from any taunt attempt made through poisoned ground", and the kiting plan generally assumes Shen cannot stay on you once the taunt ends.
audit.why: Twilight Assault slows every enemy it collided with while they are running away from Shen. Move Quick is a move-speed buff, not a dash or a cleanse — a Shen who lands Q on the way out keeps pace with the escape. "Guarantees" is the wrong word and it will get players killed at the end of trades they thought they had won.
audit.corrected: Twilight Assault slows you specifically while you run from him, so Move Quick alone does not guarantee the exit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shen's Q is referred to only as "his Q empowered auto" and "his Q empowered follow-up" — never named, and its damage type never stated.
audit.why: Twilight Assault deals damage based on the target's maximum health and is greatly empowered when the spirit blade collides with an enemy champion first. The collision condition is the readable tell: a blade recalled through you is the empowered version, one recalled through empty ground is not.
audit.corrected: Twilight Assault — max-health damage, empowered only when the recalled blade passes through a champion.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ki Barrier is never mentioned in either layer.
audit.why: Shen gains a shield after casting any spell, and the effect's cooldown is reduced whenever he affects other champions. Against a poke champion whose damage arrives in small repeated ticks, a shield on that kind of rotation absorbs a real fraction of the chip — it is why Teemo poke feels less productive here than the health bars suggest it should.
audit.corrected: Every spell he casts refreshes a Ki Barrier shield, so short poke trades net far less than they look like they do.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid opens "Levels 4-5 are your clearest poke window: Q is approaching max rank".
audit.why: Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds at every rank, so ranking it never changes how often you can poke, and rank 5 needs level 9 regardless. The number that genuinely changes across this window is Spirit's Refuge dropping from 16s toward 13s.
audit.corrected: Blinding Dart is 7s at every rank; what moves at 4-5 is his Spirit's Refuge cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Stand United is described as "up" or "on cooldown" four times without a number, in an entry whose entire late game is built on managing it.
audit.why: Stand United is 200/180/160s. At rank 1 that is over three minutes of split-push freedom after he uses it — a completely different macro decision from the vague "when his R is down" the entry currently offers.
audit.corrected: Stand United is 200 seconds at rank 1; that is the length of your split window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Teemo's Q is written "Blinding Shot" in spikes[2] and wants.you[0].
audit.why: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json gives slot Q as "Blinding Dart".
Not a real item; the full layer of this dataset uses Liandry's Torment.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.phases[0].why says "AA-poke + E poison wins almost every melee level 1" while content.win[0] is "Shen" and the content early paragraph explains that Spirit's Refuge takes the first trade off him.
audit.why: The two layers disagree about who owns level 1, and the full layer's stated reason is the one the matchup contradicts — auto-poke is exactly what Shen answers.
audit.corrected: Level 1 goes to Shen: the bubble blocks the autos that carry Teemo's damage.

notes:
The single most useful thing missing from this matchup is that Spirit's Refuge blocks basic attacks and not spells. Both layers currently read as though the bubble turns Teemo off entirely, when in fact his Q keeps working at full effect the whole time. That distinction is likely templated across other Teemo-vs-Shen-style entries (anything with an attack-block), so it is worth a wider grep.

The 18-second figure in mid was attached to the wrong ability — it is Shadow Dash's cooldown, not Spirit's Refuge's. Every trade window the paragraph recommends was therefore several seconds too loose.

Shadow Dash costs 150 energy, which is stated in the corrected cooldowns block as a raw fact. Shen's energy pool size is not in the kit file, so no claim is made here about whether he can chain E into Q — that would need the wiki.
